reason: The ceramic blocks are the local material for the root medium, and the wash bench is the relevant processing station.
expectation: The bench will prepare clean porous ceramic medium, possibly using the drinking water.

effect: The washed ceramic is now suitable growing medium, ready to go into the beds.
reaction: The leach check and removal of sharp fines make the preparation feel physically grounded.
reason: The goal is to fill the beds with the prepared medium.
expectation: The porous medium will fill the beds while leaving air spaces for roots.

effect: The beds are filled with porous medium, and the next goal is to water their shared loop.
reaction: The distinction between air spaces and dry medium makes the next step clear.
reason: The drinking water supply can fill the dry beds and their connected irrigation loop.
expectation: Water will enter the shared reservoir and circulate through the beds.

effect: The shared irrigation loop is working, though the lettuce shelf still needs a wick; the chapter is complete.
reaction: The distinction between the watered beds and the still-dry lettuce shelf was a useful, slightly surprising detail.

mostWorthwhile.text: Preparing the ceramic medium was most worthwhile: breaking, washing and checking it explained how the material could support drainage and root aeration.

leastWorthwhile.text: Filling the beds was the least distinctive passage; it was clear and useful progress, but largely confirmed the expected next step.

surprise.text: I expected the shared loop to water all the beds, but the lettuce shelf remains dry and needs a wick.

arbitrary.text: Nothing felt particularly arbitrary; each action followed clearly from the goal and available materials.

continue.text: Yes. I would be curious to see how the lettuce wick and the rest of the growing system are completed, especially if the practical explanations continue.
